text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Three Palestinians die in Hebron riots.
- Clinton says decent chance peace talks will resume.
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu calls for restraint.
- Pope clears way for canonisation of Jewish-born nun.
- Hebrew University students protest continued use of book written in 1950s by Carl Frankenstein they believe is biased against Jews who immigrated to Israel from Arab countries.
- Infrastructure Minister Sharon backs banning sale of land to foreigners.
- Elta Electronics wins $70 million contract with Britain's air force.
- Houston's Apache Corp says it has struck oil in Egypt's Western Desert and production to begin this summer.
HAARETZ
- Three Palestinians killed in Hebron; warnings of attacks against Jewish settlers.
- American officials say Clinton-Netanyahu meeting was difficult. They are not satisfied.
- Eleven youths arrested in Jordan on suspicion of planning attack on Israeli embassy there.
- Teacher at elementary school suspected of sexually assaulting girl students.
- State prosecutor: level of police investigations is poor.
- French firm to stop producing abortion pill after pressure from anti-abortion groups.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Terror will increase after Hebron clashes; source close to Netanyahu says that some of the American ideas are dangerous.
- Turkish president refused to shake Israeli foreign minister's hand; in the end they hugged.
- Father of woman who in 1980s supposedly lured Israeli Vanunu convicted of passing Israeli nuclear secrets is identified.
- Man who was briefly appointed attorney general in January in affair that spurred commission to set procedure for attorney general appointment is to be on commission.
MAARIV
- Concern Palestinian uprising is renewing; Israeli army reinforces forces in occupied territories.
- Chemi Shalev interpretation: Return to the time of the stone and the rifle.
- Bonuses continue at banks; Hapoalim CEO gets 693,000 shekels ($1=3.39 shekels)
- Ethiopian immigrant youths: Police beat us and called us stinking niggers.
GLOBES
- Justice Ministry retreats, decides private companies do not have to publish company reports.
- Bank Leumi gives Gila Maor bonus of 383,500 shekels.
- Dollar at another peak, 3.389 shekels.
